questions.prompt: Which keyword is used for a counting loop in C#?
questions.explanation: The for keyword creates a counting loop with initialization, condition, and iterator expressions.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: for (int i = 0; i < 3; _____ ) { Console.WriteLine(i); }
Arrange these expressions to create a backward counting for loop from 5 to 1.
What happens if the initialization expression is omitted?
options: The variable must be declared beforehand
questions.explanation: If initialization is omitted, the loop variable must already exist outside the for header.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: for ( _____ ; i < 5; i++) { ... }
Write a for loop that prints even numbers from 0 to 10 (inclusive), each on a new line.
Which part of the for loop runs after each iteration of the body?
questions.explanation: The iterator expression executes after the body and before the next condition check.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: for (int i = 0; i < 5; _____ ) { ... }
Arrange the execution sequence of a for loop.
Can all three expressions in a for loop header be empty?
options: No, at least one is required
Only the iterator can be empty
questions.explanation: All three expressions are optional. An empty header (for (;;)) creates an infinite loop.
